**(i)** The cumulative distribution function, $F$, of a random variable $X$ is defined by

$$F(x) = \begin{cases} 0, & x < 1, \\ \dfrac{1}{4}, & 1 \le x < 2, \\ \dfrac{3}{4}, & 2 \le x < 3, \\ \dfrac{63}{64}, & 3 \le x < 4, \\ 1, & 4 \le x. \end{cases}$$

Calculate
incertitudes: Question 4 : les points imprimés sont (4, 6, 3) pour 13 au total, un par partie (i), (ii), (iii). Portés par i.a, ii.a et iii ; (i)(b) et (ii)(b) n'ont pas de points propres.

Question 4 (ii) : les pourcentages sont calculés avec la loi normale centrée réduite : (a) 26.6 %, (b) 25.2 % (valeurs de table interpolées 0.9651 - 0.7131 = 0.2520 ; calcul exact 0.2519). Question 4 (iii) : $z = 1.645$ lu dans la table ; le résultat est 399.37 g (399.368 avec le $z$ exact).

Question 4 (i) : $F$ est une fonction en escalier, donc $X$ est discrète (valeurs 1, 2, 3, 4 de probabilités $\frac14, \frac12, \frac{15}{64}, \frac1{64}$, de somme 1) ; la fonction imprimée est cohérente.

questions.corrige_markdown:
$F$ is a step function, so $X$ is discrete and $P(X = 3)$ is the size of the jump of $F$ at $x = 3$:

$$P(X = 3) = F(3) - \lim_{x \to 3^-} F(x) = \frac{63}{64} - \frac{3}{4} = \frac{63}{64} - \frac{48}{64} = \frac{15}{64}$$

**$P(X = 3) = \dfrac{15}{64} \approx 0.234$.**

For a cumulative distribution function, $P(a < X \le b) = F(b) - F(a)$:

$$P(1 < X \le 3) = F(3) - F(1) = \frac{63}{64} - \frac{1}{4} = \frac{63}{64} - \frac{16}{64} = \frac{47}{64}$$

(Check with the probabilities: $P(X = 2) + P(X = 3) = \dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{15}{64} = \dfrac{47}{64}$.)

**$P(1 < X \le 3) = \dfrac{47}{64} \approx 0.734$.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
**(ii)** The masses, $M$, of cubes of soap produced by a certain machine are normally distributed with mean 400 g and standard deviation 1.6 g. By using the cumulative distribution function of the standard normal distribution, find the percentage of the cubes that will weigh

(a) less than 399 g,
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Model:** $M \sim N(400,\ 1.6^2)$. Standardise with $Z = \dfrac{M - 400}{1.6} \sim N(0, 1)$, and let $\Phi$ be the cumulative distribution function of $Z$.

$$z = \frac{399 - 400}{1.6} = -0.625$$

$$P(M < 399) = \Phi(-0.625) = 1 - \Phi(0.625) = 1 - 0.7340 = 0.2660$$

(table: $\Phi(0.62) = 0.7324$, $\Phi(0.63) = 0.7357$, interpolated $\Phi(0.625) \approx 0.7340$)

**About $26.6\%$ of the cubes weigh less than 399 g.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **(iii)** The machine develops a fault that affects only the mean mass of the cubes. On investigation, technicians discover that $95\%$ of the cubes produced weigh less than 402 g. What is the new mean mass?
questions.corrige_markdown:
The fault changes only the mean: the new model is $M \sim N(\mu,\ 1.6^2)$ with the standard deviation still 1.6 g, and $P(M < 402) = 0.95$.

From the table of the standard normal distribution, $\Phi(z) = 0.95$ gives $z = 1.645$. Hence

$$\frac{402 - \mu}{1.6} = 1.645 \;\Rightarrow\; 402 - \mu = 1.6 \times 1.645 = 2.632$$

$$\mu = 402 - 2.632 = 399.368$$

**The new mean mass is about $399.37$ g** (the mean has dropped by about 0.63 g).
